subject: Planned: us-nw1 rolling driver swap & eviction mitigation (Aug 18 maintenance window)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <ops@ivorybank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Planned: us-nw1 rolling driver swap & eviction mitigation (Aug 18 maintenance window)

Hi Claire —

Quick heads-up from the infra team: we plan a rolling driver swap in the us-nw1 (Northern California) region on Tue, Aug 18 between 00:00–06:00 UTC (Mon Aug 17 17:00–23:00 PDT local). This is a targeted maintenance to swap a kernel driver build that has shown a small but growing risk of transient GPU allocation eviction under heavy preemption bursts.

Impact summary (short):
- Staged node swaps (waves) across availability groups; each pod will be cordoned and drained; expected per-node disruption: 30–90s for in-flight tokenized requests in edge cases.
- We will maintain rolling capacity by keeping a hot pool and enabling cross-region routing for non-latency-sensitive traffic.
- Customers on Dedicated can opt out by pinning instances; see attached checklist and schedule.

What we need from you:
1) Ack the window (or propose alternatives within 72 hours).
2) Confirm any critical pinned workloads we should exclude.

Attachments: pre-rollout-checklist.pdf, staged-schedule.csv — these include the exact shard order and the fallback playbook.

Operational mitigations we will run:
- Automated health checks and automatic fallback to previous driver variant for nodes failing readiness probes.
- Short-circuit routing to Redwood Dedicated pools or eu-west fallback for heavy jobs if eviction rate spikes above 0.5%.
- Real-time dashboard and Slack bridge to your oncall channel (oncall-ivory@ivorybank.com).

Marissa / Lauren — I included the playbook and a conservative schedule. Please review the staged steps (preflight hooks, drain grace seconds, retry/backoff settings) and flag anything we should change for Ivory Bank.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Production Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: pre-rollout-checklist.pdf (PDF, 42KB), staged-schedule.csv (CSV, 2KB)

From: Claire Huang <ops@ivorybank.com>

Subject: Re: Planned: us-nw1 rolling driver swap & eviction mitigation (Aug 18 maintenance window)

Rishi —

Thanks for the heads-up. A couple of quick Qs from our side:
1) Session persistence: if a request is routed to an alternate region during a short eviction, will user sessions or streaming responses resume or restart? We have some long-poll streams for risk scoring.
2) Cache/KV impacts: does the KV cache (prefix cache) get invalidated or warmed automatically after a node rejoins?
3) SLA credits: if we see increased error rates or elevated latencies for >30m, what’s the escalation path and SLAs?

We can OK the window provisionally if the streaming behavior is safe; can you provide the fallback playbook in plain text (for our auditors)? Also, point of contact during the window — will you be the primary?

Claire Huang
Sr. ProdOps, Ivory Bank
ops@ivorybank.com

Oncall: oncall-ivory@ivorybank.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <ops@ivorybank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, support@acmecloud.com
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Planned: us-nw1 rolling driver swap & eviction mitigation (Aug 18 maintenance window)

Claire —

Thanks — answers inline and appended the plain-text fallback playbook (also attached as fallback-playbook.txt).

1) Streaming/session behavior:
- Short-lived (sub-5s) interruptions: clients will see transient TCP resets or streaming deltas and should auto-reconnect. We recommend using idempotent tokens for resumable streams; for current Ivory streams we will keep the LB affinity long enough for a reconnect window (60s) before migrating.
- Long sessions (>5m): we will avoid routing these mid-request; if a node shows instability we will mark it drain-only for new sessions.

2) KV/prefix cache:
- We maintain a persistent KV tier; in-memory prefix caches are opportunistic. When a node rejoins, the cache is warmed by traffic; critical cache entries are preserved in the persistent tier. No forced global invalidation.

3) SLA & escalation:
- If error rate >0.5% for a sustained 30m window we will (a) open an incident in OPS-4218 and (b) trigger automatic failover to dedicated pool for your account; you will be eligible for SLA review and potential credit per the contract.
- POC: I'll be the primary lead during the window (Slack: @rishi), Marissa will handle rollback coordination. Oncall contact is also copied.

Fallback playbook (excerpt):
- Preflight: run preflight checklist (attached). Confirm health checks pass on new driver build.
- Wave 1: cordon + drain 5% of nodes; validate 10 min of stable metrics (errors, evictions, gpu_alloc_rate).
- If eviction rate >0.5% or regeneration errors >0.2% for 10 min -> abort wave, rollback driver on that node, open incident, and enable cross-region routing for queued work.
- Final: post-rollout smoke 60m, collect perf dumps and attach to OPS ticket.

I also attached a tightened schedule (staged-schedule.csv) that shows the wave order. Jira link: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/OPS-4218.

If that works, please reply with an ACK and list any pinned workloads you want excluded.

Regards,
Rishi

--
Attachments: fallback-playbook.txt (TXT, 6KB)
